name: Custom Promotional Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Promotional Stickers for Giveaways and Campaigns
seoDescription: Custom promotional stickers for giveaways, events, mailers and box seals. Paper, BOPP or vinyl, singles or sheets, QR codes and offers in full color.
tagline: Campaign stickers people keep: slogans, offers, event art and QR codes on paper, BOPP or vinyl.
quickAnswer: Custom promotional stickers are printed stickers used as giveaways and advertising: slogans, mascots, event artwork, QR codes and offers rather than a plain logo. They are printed in full color on paper, BOPP or vinyl, as singles, sheets or rolls, for brands, venues and event organizers handing them out in volume. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.

sections.h2: A giveaway sticker only works if someone wants to stick it somewhere
sections.html:
Ask what a stranger would put on a water bottle. Usually it is a joke, a mascot, a piece of artwork or a slogan from a place they like, and only sometimes a bare logo. That is the difference between this product and its sibling, the die cut logo sticker page. Logo stickers are the brand mark, cut to its outline, used on packaging and products you already sell. Promotional stickers are campaign pieces: they carry an offer, a date, a QR code or a design made to be collected, and they are produced in bigger, cheaper runs because most of them are given away.

We print them for breweries and coffee roasters, bands and venues, trade show booths, nonprofits, schools, app launches and direct-mail inserts. Many start as a sheet of three or four designs so a customer can pick the one they like.

sections.h2: Pick the stock by where the sticker ends up
sections.html:
The cheapest stock is not always the cheapest campaign. A paper sticker that peels off a laptop in a week stops advertising; a vinyl one keeps working for years. Decide by the likely destination.

sections.h2: Singles, sheets or rolls for handing out
sections.html:
Format changes how fast you can give them away and how they look in the hand.

  • Die cut singles: one sticker on its own backing, cut to the shape of the art. The best-looking handout and the easiest to drop into an order.
  • Kiss cut sheets: three to six designs on a 4" x 6" or 5" x 7" sheet with the backing left whole. People peel what they like and keep the rest, which spreads one giveaway over several uses.
  • Rolls: hundreds of stickers on a 3" core for sealing boxes, tagging bags or tearing off at a counter.
  • Sticker packs: four or five singles bagged together as a prize or a merch item.
  • Sizes: 2" to 3" is the sweet spot for laptops and bottles; 4" and up suits bumpers and coolers; 1" to 1.5" works for box seals and mailers.

Sheets are printed as a single piece, so the per-sticker cost is lower than the same designs as singles.

sections.h2: What to print on a promotional sticker so it keeps working
sections.html: Put the thing people want in the center and the thing you want near the edge. A slogan or illustration earns the spot on the laptop; your website or handle in small type along the bottom edge comes along for the ride. A QR code needs to be at least 0.8" square with a plain border, and it should lead to a page that is still live a year later, since stickers outlast campaigns. Offer codes work on stickers tucked into orders ("10% off your next order: STICKER10"), less so on giveaways that get stuck to a bottle and never read again. Dates belong on event stickers only; everything else should be undated so leftovers are still useful next season. The Die Cut Stickers home page shows the materials and finishes if you want a holographic or clear version of a design for the premium tier of a giveaway.

sections.h2: Planning a sticker campaign from first draft to first box
sections.html:
1. Decide the job of the sticker: a thank-you in every order, a trade show handout, a merch item, or a box seal. That sets the stock and the format.
  2. Set the quantity by how many hands it will reach, not by the price break. The minimum is 100 stickers, and a mailer insert program usually needs 1,000 or more.
  3. Send artwork as a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size. Free design support can turn a logo and a slogan into a finished sticker.
  4. Approve the free digital proof. We show the cut line and any QR code at actual size so you can scan it from the screen.
  5. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after approval, with free FedEx shipping in the United States. Say if the stickers have to meet an event date and rush is available.

Pricing starts at $0.30 per sticker and falls steeply with quantity, so a 2,500 run on paper often costs little more than 1,000. Stickers that double as box seals can match the brand labels on your cartons, and our custom packaging label range is printed on the same press so the colors agree.

sections.h2: Mistakes that waste a promotional run
sections.html: Fine type is the big one. Anything under 6 pt on a 2" sticker is unreadable once printed, so drop the legal line or move it to the website. Dark art on dark backgrounds disappears on a black laptop; add a white or light keyline. Odd shapes with thin spikes tear on the peel, so round the points on a die cut design. And the last mistake is ordering too few: a box of 100 at a two-day trade show is gone by lunchtime on the first day, so plan for the footfall and keep the leftovers for the next show, which is why undated artwork pays off.

faqs.q: What size should a promotional sticker be for laptops and water bottles?
faqs.a: 2" to 3" on the longest side. That reads from across a cafe table, fits beside other stickers on a laptop lid and wraps a bottle without creasing. Go to 4" for bumpers and coolers, and down to 1.5" for box seals and mailer inserts where space is tight.

faqs.q: Is paper or vinyl better for giveaway stickers?
faqs.a: Vinyl for anything you hope people will stick to a laptop, bottle or car, because it survives washing and sun for years. Paper for inserts, handouts and box seals, where it is cheaper in volume and the sticker lives a short life on cardboard or in a drawer.

faqs.q: Can I put several designs on one promotional sticker sheet?
faqs.a: Yes. A 4" x 6" or 5" x 7" kiss cut sheet holds three to six designs on a shared backing. The sheet prints as one piece, so the cost per design is lower than ordering each as singles, and the person receiving it can peel the ones they want.

faqs.q: Will a QR code on a promotional sticker scan reliably?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is printed at least 0.8" square with a plain margin and kept to black on white or a light color. We show the code at actual size on the proof so you can scan it from your screen before the run. Point it at a page you will keep live.

faqs.q: How many promotional stickers do I need for a trade show?
faqs.a: Count the visitors you expect to speak with and double it, since stickers get taken in twos and threes. For a two-day regional show that is often 1,000 to 2,500. The minimum run is 100, and undated artwork means any leftovers go to the next show.

faqs.q: Can promotional stickers carry a discount code for the next order?
faqs.a: Yes, and it works best on stickers packed into orders rather than handed out at events. Keep the code short and the sticker 2" or larger so the text stays readable. We can print the same art with several codes if you track channels separately.

faqs.q: Do advertising stickers need a laminate?
faqs.a: On paper, no; they are meant for dry, short-term use. On vinyl, a laminate is worth it: it keeps scuffs off the print on a laptop, stops fading on a car and lets the sticker go through a dishwasher on a bottle. Choose matte laminate if you want less glare.

faqs.q: Can I order promotional stickers with removable adhesive for a venue?
faqs.a: Yes. Removable adhesive suits stickers handed out at a venue or school where they may end up on walls, lockers and windows and need to come off clean. Permanent adhesive suits bumpers, coolers and packaging where the sticker should stay put through weather.

faqs.q: What file do you need for a promotional sticker design?
faqs.a: A vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or PDF) is best, because a sticker die cut to the art outline needs clean edges. A 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size also works for printed shapes. If you only have a logo and a slogan, free design support can build the sticker for you.

faqs.q: How long does a promotional sticker run take before an event?
faqs.a: Allow 5 to 7 business days of production after you approve the proof, plus delivery, for a total of 8 to 10 business days with free FedEx shipping in the United States. If the event is sooner, ask about rush production when you request the quote.

faqs.q: Can marketing stickers be printed in holographic or clear material?
faqs.a: Yes. Holographic film suits a premium tier of a giveaway or a limited run, and clear vinyl works for a design that should look printed onto the bottle or window. Both cost more than paper, so most campaigns print the bulk on paper or vinyl and a smaller run on the special stock.

faqs.q: Does the price of promotional stickers drop at higher quantities?
faqs.a: Yes, sharply. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and the per-piece cost falls as the run grows, because setup is spread over more stickers and larger runs move to offset printing. A 2,500 paper run often costs little more than 1,000, so quote the larger number before deciding.
